text.insert: Returns codebases sorted by name. Repository registrations that resolve to the same remote use registration's remote equality rules, including GitHub HTTPS/SSH spellings, trailing slashes,

suffixes, GitHub repository-path case variants, and equivalent local paths. Repository paths on other hosts remain case-sensitive. Only the most recently updated row for each resolved remote is returned. Folder registrations and rows without a repository URL remain separate.

rows.insert: Cancel a running workflow: a run this server executes stops at its next status check; a run another process owns has that owner stopped first. Returns
with the reason, and leaves the run unchanged, when no owner answers (abandon it once its process is gone) or the owner cannot be stopped;

Resume a failed or paused workflow. A run started outside the web UI resumes on the server and returns

with the reason, leaving the run unchanged, when its resource is full: a paused run that is ready to continue keeps its place and a continuation host continues it, and a failed run stays failed until it is resumed again. A run started from a web conversation reports the same wait in that conversation
Abandon a run (running, paused, or failed); stops a live detached owner first, attempts to cancel discovered
descendants except completed and cancelled runs within the
, and attempts to remove the worktrees those runs created, keeping their branches. Owner warnings retain affected checkouts: inspect them (
when output is still held), resolve the warning, then abandon the cancelled run again to retry removal. Returns

with the reason, and leaves the run unchanged, when an owner answers but cannot be stopped or the run cannot be abandoned. A silent descendant also retains its checkout and the selected root's checkout, even if the root's owner stopped; each descendant needs its own owner check. If the selected sub-run has no answering endpoint, cancellation succeeds but its subtree's owned checkouts remain: silence does not prove the enclosing execution stopped. Inspect the owning execution and stop or abandon it only if you intend to stop its whole scope; repeated child-only abandonment may still retain the checkouts.

text.insert: These are Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoints -- connect with

Create a Conversation and Send a Message

# 1. Create a conversation
CONV_ID=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3090/api/conversations \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}' | jq -r '.conversationId')

# 2. Send a message
curl -X POST http://localhost:3090/api/conversations/$CONV_ID/message \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "/status"}'

# 3. Poll for messages
curl http://localhost:3090/api/conversations/$CONV_ID/messages
Run a Workflow via the API

# 1. Create a conversation scoped to a codebase
CONV_ID=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3090/api/conversations \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"codebaseId": "your-codebase-id"}' | jq -r '.conversationId')

# 2. Start the workflow
curl -X POST http://localhost:3090/api/workflows/archon-investigate/run \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"message\": \"Why does login fail after a password reset?\", \"conversationId\": \"$CONV_ID\"}"

# 3. Monitor via SSE
curl -N http://localhost:3090/api/stream/$CONV_ID
